title: Finite free retract tensors preserve base flatness
statement: Let $C$ be a small site, $R,A$ sheaves of commutative rings and $\alpha:R\to A$ a ring-sheaf map. Let $P,N$ be sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $m\in\mathbb N$ and $\iota:P\to A^{\oplus m}$, $\pi:A^{\oplus m}\to P$ satisfy $\iota\pi=1_P$. If $N$, restricted along $\alpha$, is a flat $R$-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then the ordinary tensor $P\otimes_A N$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], restricted along $\alpha$, is a flat $R$-module sheaf. No flatness of $A$ over $R$ is assumed. This includes rank zero and the empty site.

source.place: Tags 03EU (direct sums), 00HD (mono criterion, hence retract stability), and the finite-free tensor calculation in 0DJQ; source-library ObjectProperty.flat_of_retract

proof.text: Scalar restriction leaves the abelian sheaf unchanged. The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves and reflects colimits, so scalar restriction preserves coproducts. Right tensoring preserves coproducts by the tensor-Hom adjunction. The tensor of a free module with N is therefore the coproduct of m copies of N, using the tensor unit isomorphism.

After scalar restriction the preceding isomorphism identifies the ambient free tensor with a finite coproduct of flat modules. Apply isFlat_coproduct and transport flatness through this isomorphism. In the closed symmetric category the right-tensor exactness predicate implies ObjectProperty.flat by the braiding.

Apply right tensoring and scalar restriction to the given inclusion and retraction. Functor.map_comp and map_id preserve their identity composite. ObjectProperty.flat_of_retract transfers flatness to the restricted P tensor N; take its right-tensor exactness component. This step uses the already proved source-library retract theorem, whose proof follows the mono criterion of flatness.
